html:
A chain of dams, sluices and storm surge barriers built in the southwest Netherlands to protect the land from the sea. Most of it was built after the North Sea flood of 1953 and finished in 1997.

The southwest of the country is a delta where the Rhine, Maas and Scheldt rivers meet the sea. The 1953 flood broke the old dikes there and drowned some 1,800 people. A plan drawn up after the flood became law in 1958. Closing the sea inlets shortened the coast to be defended by hundreds of kilometres.

The best known parts are the barriers. In the Eastern Scheldt, protests from fishermen and nature groups led to a barrier of huge sliding gates that stay open and close only in storms, finished in 1986, so the tides and shellfish survive. The last piece, the Maeslant barrier near Rotterdam, has two huge arms, each about 210 metres long, that swing shut across the shipping channel.

With the earlier Zuiderzee Works, the Delta Works are a symbol of the Dutch struggle with water.
sum: A chain of dams, sluices and storm surge barriers built in the southwest Netherlands to protect the land from the sea. Most of it was built after the North Sea flood of 1953 and finished in 1997.
